tickets.title: 11th Street e-bike storage and delivery worker congestion
tickets.requester: Unnamed public speaker (11th Street resident); Keith Powers (Assembly Member); District Manager
tickets.summary: Over 100 electric delivery bikes are stored on and around the sidewalk at 11th Street and First Avenue around the clock, obstructing businesses, residents and the sidewalk, with a fire-hazard concern. The district office has worked on the issue since February 2024, and the 9th Precinct plans enforcement on October 7 that could confiscate unlegally parked bikes, while groups ask for tagging and notice instead. Action: District office to continue coordinating with the precinct, elected officials and worker groups on enforcement notice and suitable parking sites for the bikes.

tickets.title: Seward Park drug activity and dark park lighting
tickets.requester: Board member (unnamed); Parks committee; Niles Robinson (liaison, Manhattan Borough President's office)
tickets.summary: Residents and park groups report increased drug use, homelessness and needle litter in Seward Park, including the Lower East Side Ecology Center building next to a frequently used bathroom. A board member also noted poorly lit dark spots in the park where drug use can go unseen. The Borough President's office is monitoring the situation with the 7th Precinct, and the district manager has mentioned outreach and police presence. Action: Residents should report out-of-service lights to 311, and the district office should follow up with the 7th Precinct, Parks and DOT on enforcement, lighting and whether mobile crisis teams could respond instead of police.

tickets.title: Free public restroom pilot locations in district
tickets.summary: The city is installing 17 free public bathrooms citywide as a one-year pilot, including one near Delancey Plaza and one at Cooper Square and East Sixth Street, with DOT as lead agency. The committee raised concerns about access, who can use the restrooms, and emergency calls, and the office is still working with community partners on locations. Action: Committee to bring a resolution next month setting out how the board wants the pilot handled.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP community market safeguards
tickets.summary: The board passed two resolutions asking the EDC to shape the Essex Market RFP so the market stays a community market. At a joint meeting with the economic development subcommittee, EDC could not say how the resolutions were incorporated, and the RFP is due to go out at the end of the month. Action: Land use committee to meet with EDC later this week and push to postpone issuing the RFP until the community's requests are included.

tickets.title: Manhattan Bridge exits and Canal Street redesign update
tickets.summary: The board has passed multiple resolutions on safety at the foot of the Manhattan Bridge exits, and a recent crash and death prompted renewed concern. The Canal Street redesign project has not had an update since January. Action: A letter was sent to the Mayor and DOT reiterating community concerns and asking for an update on the Canal Street redesign.

tickets.title: Congestion pricing impact on FDR Drive follow-up
tickets.summary: The board previously passed a resolution on possible congestion impacts on the FDR from congestion pricing, and the MTA released an air quality report. The board member asked whether the projected congestion actually occurred and whether reporting is planned. Action: Follow up with MTA and DOT on whether FDR congestion materialized and request any planned reporting.

tickets.title: Transit equity analysis with IBO
tickets.summary: The committee met with the Independent Budget Office over the summer about whether the district receives its fair share of transportation resources compared with other districts. From about ten ideas, the committee narrowed the research to three priorities, including cross-town buses and neighborhood parking locations. Action: Continue the IBO research on cross-town buses and neighborhood parking, and report results back to the committee.

tickets.title: Third Avenue L stop closure pilot proposal
tickets.summary: A public speaker argued from MTA data that closing the Third Avenue L stop would save riders about 1,800 hours a day because only 5% of riders board or alight there. The stop is not a transfer station and is not wheelchair accessible. Action: Refer the proposal to the transportation committee and ask the board to request a pilot closure of the Third Avenue stop with the MTA.

tickets.title: MetroCard transit cost help for uptown travel
tickets.summary: A public attendee asked whether MetroCards or OMNY-based support could offset transit costs for people traveling to the immigrant welcome center at 125th Street, a trip that can take an hour with multiple transfers. The liaison said the question would be raised with the office. Action: Raise the transit cost offset question with the Borough President's office liaison.

tickets.title: NYCHA residents need food and necessities
tickets.summary: A public speaker from NYCHA housing described hardship in the community, including lack of food, water, necessities and work, and said drugs and toxicity are a problem. He also asked for accessible communication for deaf and hard-of-hearing residents. Action: Refer the request for food, necessities and communication access to the appropriate social services agencies.

tickets.title: Proposed roller rink on East River Pier
tickets.location_raw: East River Pier across from the Katherine Slip Mall
tickets.summary: A public speaker proposed a 300,000 square foot, three-story indoor roller skating facility on the East River Pier, with $8 admission and projected 250 to 500 jobs. The speaker cited the loss of historic rinks to real estate costs. Action: Board to review the pier development proposal and determine whether to request a land use process or agency response.

tickets.title: Mobile voting option for CEC elections
tickets.summary: The committee presented a resolution supporting a mobile-first voting pilot for Community Education Council elections, because turnout has been around 2% and many households are mobile-only. Speakers also raised outreach to immigrant families, eligibility clarity, and equity in who joins CEC councils. Action: Board to vote on the resolution urging the NYC Department of Education to pilot mobile voting and expand multilingual parent outreach.

tickets.title: Bylaws attendance procedure revisions
tickets.summary: Proposed bylaw changes would address attendance by sending a letter and inviting a member to meet with the executive committee after excess absences, rather than waiting for a removal process. The changes also remove attendance from the removal process and require public members to follow conflict of interest policies. Action: Full board to vote on the proposed bylaw changes at the October meeting, with notice sent at least 28 days in advance.

tickets.title: Board training on SLA, Robert's Rules and office procedures
tickets.summary: The board chair plans trainings on SLA, Robert's Rules and office procedures, with dates still to be announced. The chair wants more deliberate questions from members and asked for training topic requests. Action: Board chair to set training dates and members to email CB3 chair with training topics.

tickets.title: Second vice chair election result
tickets.summary: Candidates Daniel Tano and Zachary Thomas gave speeches for second vice chair, and members voted by ballot. Daniel Tano received 25 votes and Zachary Thomas received 14. Action: None; Daniel Tano was elected second vice chair.

tickets.title: Budget priorities ranking vote in October
tickets.summary: Each committee will vote on expense and capital budget priorities for city agencies in October, after district managers met with over 20 agencies about program cuts and funding gaps. The district manager explained the ranking process and gave an example about summer youth employment. Action: Committees to vote on ranked district needs and budget priorities for each agency in October.

tickets.title: Draft housing plan comments and affordable housing
tickets.summary: The city's draft housing plan proposes about 7,000 units over five years, but 75% are market rate, while the board's top priority is affordable housing. The board had already submitted comments on the draft plan using the district needs statement. Action: None; the board submitted comments, and committees should take positions proactively on future plans.

tickets.title: Liquor license denial for 11 Allen Street
tickets.summary: The board considered a full liquor license application for a location at 11 Allen Street by an operator formerly of Time Cafe, and a committee had voted 3 to 2 for a conditional approval with stipulations. A board member moved for a straight denial, arguing the area is saturated and the prior location caused problems. The board voted 20 to deny, 10 against and 9 abstaining, and members were urged to attend the SLA hearing to oppose it. Action: None by the board; the board voted to deny, and community members should attend the SLA hearing.

tickets.title: Resolution wording corrections for Tea House and Cozy Cafe
tickets.summary: The August resolutions for Tea House and Cozy Cafe mistakenly referred to full on-premises licenses when the applications were for beer and wine licenses. The Cozy Cafe owners are splitting, and the new location plans no DJs under the committee negotiation. Action: Correct the resolution language for Tea House item 10 and Cozy Cafe item 3 to read beer and wine licenses.
